properties.decision:
THE RULING, for a genre rather than for two files. Anthony, 2026-08-19: *"restore and park two field reports."*

**THE GENRE:** a dated report ABOUT this system's behaviour, written from outside its development — an agent-authored field report from a project that uses reflow2, a bug report, an incident write-up, a user complaint, a beamline observation, a vendor's test certificate. Its defining property is that it is a FROZEN OBSERVATION: true of a moment, and it must not be revised as the design moves.

**WHAT TO DO WITH ONE:** REGISTER the Artifact so the design knows the evidence exists and where it lives, draw NO claim edge, and GOVERN it by this ruling with `ruling: parks`. Detectors then report it as parked and COUNT it in `swept.parked`, rather than filing a deliberate state as a structural defect.

**BOTH ALTERNATIVES ARE FALSE, and this is why the ruling is needed rather than a convention:**
· **A `DOCUMENTS` edge would lie about the direction of obligation.** DOCUMENTS means "this file describes the design and would be WRONG if it drifted out of step with it". A field report is the opposite: it is correct precisely by NOT tracking the design. Under DOCUMENTS, every future design change would read as staling a report that is simply history.
· **Leaving it unregistered loses the evidence.** The file exists, it is cited, and a design that cannot say where its field evidence lives has to rediscover it. This is the state the graph was in between `fbc8e55` and this ruling.
· **Deleting it is the worst of the three**, because it is the one that LOOKS clean: the defect count falls, the gate goes green, and the design quietly stops knowing what it was told.

**THE ONE EDGE THAT IS TRUE:** none of REALIZES / DOCUMENTS / SPECIFIES / PRODUCES / SATISFIES applies, and that is not a gap in the report — it is the accurate description of a document that implements nothing, specifies nothing and describes nothing. `parks` is how the design says so out loud instead of leaving it to be inferred from an absence.

**WHAT IT IS NOT.** Parking is not acknowledgement and not suppression. `acknowledge_defect` is per-instance and expires when the shape changes; this is a standing ruling over a genre whose shape is deliberately fixed. The parked nodes stay visible and counted — `dec:report-dont-judge` is respected, because reflow2 is reading a ruling the design already made rather than deciding anything on its own.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, named so it is not read as settling it:** whether `artifact_type` should gain a value for human evidence. It has `test_result` for the machine kind. "Attaches to nothing on purpose" is not the same claim as "this is dated evidence and it ages" — cf. `req:evidence-carries-the-date-it-was-taken`. That question stays open under `dec:idea-parks-shipped-and-was-still-not-reached-the-instruction-is-missing-where-the-person-is-stuck`.

GOVERNS, as of 2026-08-19: `art:ophyd-service-feedback-2026-08-19`, `art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-08-19`. The genre is expected to grow; new members are parked under this same ruling rather than under a new one each time.
properties.name: A dated field report is REGISTERED and PARKED — its unattached state is correct and deliberate, and neither deleting it nor giving it a DOCUMENTS edge is honest
properties.rationale: Written as a ruling over a GENRE rather than a note on two files because that is the shape the case actually has, and because per-instance acknowledgement was already judged the wrong tool for it in req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect: acknowledging findings one at a time to record one standing rule does not scale and expires on nodes whose shape is fixed on purpose. Accepted on Anthony's explicit instruction of 2026-08-19 — `parks` refuses a `proposed` ruling by design, so that a musing cannot suppress a finding, which means this decision could not have been made by the agent alone. It exists at all because the same design's own accepted requirement predicted that an agent watching the defect count would delete such documents instead, and then one did.
